key_insight: A pretrained AlphaTensor-Quantum model can be reused without retraining to optimize a broad class of quantum circuits, producing substantial T-count reductions and demonstrating generalizable, efficient circuit compression.
problem_solved: High T-counts in fault-tolerant quantum circuits drive large resource and runtime costs, and many existing optimizers are circuit-specific or require costly retraining.
method: Apply a pretrained AlphaTensor-Quantum model as a reusable optimizer to propose low‑T decompositions for arbitrary gates.
Extend the pipeline to map diverse circuits into Clifford+T form and perform cost-aware search/refinement (heuristics/graph search) without retraining.
Benchmark automated T-count reductions across a wide range of circuits to validate generalizability and quantify resource savings.
impact: Cuts fault-tolerant resource overheads and speeds up quantum algorithm deployment, making quantum routines more practical for AI/ML researchers and hybrid workflows; reduces iteration time by avoiding retraining.
visual_elements: Bar chart: before vs after T-count across representative benchmark circuits (absolute and % reduction).
Pipeline diagram: pretrained AlphaTensor-Quantum → gate mapping → cost-aware refinement → optimized circuit.
Scatter plot: T-count reduction vs circuit size/depth to show scaling and generalizability.
Icon set: reduced qubit/time/resource icons to communicate practical savings at a glance.
paper_title: Reusability report: Optimizing T count in general quantum circuits with AlphaTensor-Quantum
paper_authors: Remmy Zen, Maximilian Nägele, Florian Marquardt
